title: Smart warehousing
introen: Economical coverage for conventional racks up to 8 m, automated-storage structures and warehouse mezzanine supports.

scenes.title: Pallet racking up to 8 m
scenes.en: Provide basic inclination coverage across conventional pallet-rack rows up to 8 m high where an economical multi-point installation is the priority. Associate each reading with the aisle, bay and upright, then compare it with the installation baseline. Warehouse teams can use persistent posture changes to target a closer inspection and review them alongside handling or loading records.
scenes.measureen: Inclination changes at selected pallet-rack uprights against their installation baseline.
scenes.objectiveen: Inclination changes at selected pallet-rack uprights against their installation baseline.
scenes.pointen: A rigid fixing on the selected upright, protected from pallets and forklift contact, with the same orientation convention across the rack row.
scenes.briefen: Rack height and layout, upright IDs, point count, loading patterns and the angle changes that need an inspection response.
scenes.alten: Wide warehouse aisle with conventional pallet racks, clearly visible upright frames and several levels of stored pallets.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.
scenes.heightSegment: User target segment: conventional pallet racks up to 8 m; height alone is not an engineering suitability assessment.

scenes.title: Automated storage rack frames
scenes.en: Extend basic tilt coverage to selected structural members in an automated storage and retrieval system. Link each point to its rack row, level and frame ID so the warehouse team can locate a changed reading within the larger installation. Economical multi-point coverage helps organise routine inspection records across the storage structure and compare its posture after maintenance or loading changes.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of selected automated-storage rack-frame members relative to the installation reference.
scenes.objectiveen: Local inclination of selected automated-storage rack-frame members relative to the installation reference.
scenes.pointen: An approved rigid rack upright or frame member outside stacker-crane, shuttle and service-clearance envelopes.
scenes.briefen: System layout, actual rack height, frame IDs, operating clearances, point count and the angle changes relevant to the inspection plan.
scenes.alten: Automated storage warehouse with tall rack frames, a stacker-crane aisle and the surrounding storage structure visible.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.
scenes.heightSegment: Automated-storage structures: actual project height is assessed separately; not universally limited to 8 m.

scenes.title: Drive-in racking up to 8 m
scenes.en: Follow the posture of selected uprights in drive-in pallet-rack lanes up to 8 m high. Point IDs tied to each lane make it easier to locate a changed reading within dense storage. An economical set of sensing points supports routine checks across several lanes, with the angle history reviewed alongside forklift activity, loading changes and rack inspections.
scenes.measureen: Inclination changes at selected drive-in rack uprights relative to their recorded reference.
scenes.objectiveen: Inclination changes at selected drive-in rack uprights relative to their recorded reference.
scenes.pointen: A protected rigid position on the lane’s selected upright, clear of forklift travel and pallet-support rails.
scenes.briefen: Lane layout, rack height, loading sequence, upright IDs, access clearances and the number of points needed across the storage area.
scenes.alten: Deep-lane drive-in pallet racking with an empty access lane, continuous side pallet-support rails and stored pallets visible inside the warehouse.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.
scenes.heightSegment: User target segment: drive-in racks up to 8 m; inspection purpose and relevant angle change guide selection.

scenes.title: Cantilever racking up to 8 m
scenes.en: Monitor the basic posture of cantilever-rack uprights up to 8 m high where long goods are stored across several bays. Give each point a row and column ID, then compare later readings with the installed reference. The resulting asset record helps teams focus a follow-up inspection after loading changes, a reported handling impact or relocation of the rack.
scenes.measureen: Inclination of selected cantilever-rack columns against their installation reference.
scenes.objectiveen: Inclination of selected cantilever-rack columns against their installation reference.
scenes.pointen: A rigid position on the selected column, clear of projecting arms, long goods, slings and normal loading contact.
scenes.briefen: Rack height, column and bay IDs, stored material lengths, loading arrangement and the point coverage required across the rack.
scenes.alten: Cantilever racks holding long steel tubes, with their upright columns, projecting arms and floor-mounted bases visible.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.
scenes.heightSegment: User target segment: cantilever racks up to 8 m; the image is representative rather than a measured-height installation record.

scenes.title: Mobile pallet racking up to 8 m
scenes.en: Keep a basic inclination record for mobile pallet-rack frames up to 8 m high. Associate each point with its rack block and upright so observations remain traceable when aisle arrangements change. Compare the frame under a consistent parked and loading condition, helping warehouse teams review posture changes after servicing, relocation or reported handling contact across multiple rack blocks.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of a mobile rack’s rigid structural frame under comparable parked conditions.
scenes.objectiveen: Local inclination of a mobile rack’s rigid structural frame under comparable parked conditions.
scenes.pointen: A protected member of the rack frame, away from base rails, wheel mechanisms, drives and pallet contact.
scenes.briefen: Rack-block IDs, height, parked reference condition, loading arrangement, rail clearances and the points required across the mobile storage area.
scenes.alten: Mobile pallet-racking blocks inside a warehouse, with upright frames, a storage aisle and floor rails visible.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.
scenes.heightSegment: User target segment: mobile pallet racks up to 8 m; compare like parked and loading conditions.

scenes.title: Warehouse mezzanine supports
scenes.en: Include selected mezzanine support columns in a warehouse’s economical asset-monitoring plan. A consistent column ID and installation reference make readings easier to compare across the storage floor and its supporting level. Teams can review persistent posture changes alongside layout alterations, loading records and planned inspections, using the angle record to identify the particular column that needs a closer look.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of selected warehouse-mezzanine support columns.
scenes.objectiveen: Local inclination of selected warehouse-mezzanine support columns.
scenes.pointen: A rigid column position at an approved accessible height, protected from handling contact and clear of stairs and escape routes.
scenes.briefen: Mezzanine layout, column IDs, access, loading arrangement and the inspection-scale angle changes to be reviewed.
scenes.alten: Steel warehouse mezzanine with its floor platform, support columns and access staircase shown in a wide factory interior.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.

title: Outdoor lighting & roads
introen: Basic inclination records for street lights, solar lights, traffic equipment poles and billboard supports across many locations.

scenes.title: Street-light poles
scenes.en: Add economical tilt coverage to street-light columns spread along a road, business park or residential estate. Link each point to the pole’s asset number and installation reference so changes can be located within the lighting inventory. Review a persistent departure alongside maintenance visits, reported vehicle contact and local conditions to help prioritise a field inspection across many poles.
scenes.measureen: Changes in the lighting column’s inclination relative to its recorded installation posture.
scenes.objectiveen: Changes in the lighting column’s inclination relative to its recorded installation posture.
scenes.pointen: An owner-approved rigid fixing on the column at a serviceable height, clear of access doors, cabling and routine maintenance contact.
scenes.briefen: Pole inventory, mounting arrangement, site conditions, required point count and the angle changes that should prompt a lighting-team review.
scenes.alten: Wide urban road with a row of street-light poles, visible column bases, landscaped verges and surrounding buildings.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.

scenes.title: Solar street-light poles
scenes.en: Follow the posture of solar street-light poles across dispersed paths, rural roads or industrial estates. Record the pole ID and initial inclination so the maintenance team can compare each asset with its own reference. Cost-conscious point coverage helps identify a lasting posture change after installation work or a reported impact, alongside checks of the pole, base and attached equipment.
scenes.measureen: Inclination changes of the solar-light column relative to its initial mounting reference.
scenes.objectiveen: Inclination changes of the solar-light column relative to its initial mounting reference.
scenes.pointen: A protected rigid position on the pole, below the panel assembly and clear of electrical enclosures and maintenance openings.
scenes.briefen: Pole locations, column and base arrangement, attached panel layout, point count and the maintenance records used for follow-up.
scenes.alten: Outdoor road lined with integrated solar street lights, with complete poles, solar panels, lamp heads and the surrounding route visible.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.

scenes.title: Camera & traffic poles
scenes.en: Include traffic-camera and roadside equipment poles in a basic tilt-monitoring programme. Giving every point a junction, pole and equipment ID helps the maintenance team locate a changed reading quickly within a dispersed asset list. Compare the supporting pole’s inclination with its installation baseline, then review a persistent change alongside service work, collision reports and the scheduled site inspection.
scenes.measureen: Posture changes of the supporting roadside pole at the selected mounting point.
scenes.objectiveen: Posture changes of the supporting roadside pole at the selected mounting point.
scenes.pointen: An approved rigid position on the supporting pole, clear of camera-adjustment mechanisms, electrical access and road operating clearances.
scenes.briefen: Junction and pole IDs, attachment locations, maintenance access, inventory size and the angle changes relevant to a site visit.
scenes.alten: Road junction with a traffic-camera pole and horizontal camera arm, pedestrian crossing and nearby urban buildings.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.

scenes.title: Billboard support poles
scenes.en: Record basic inclination at selected billboard support columns across an advertising estate. Link the angle reference to the sign location and support ID so maintenance teams can compare the same asset after servicing or reported contact. Economical coverage across several sites helps organise inspection priorities, with any posture change reviewed alongside the sign’s mounting, foundation and maintenance history.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination changes of the selected billboard support column.
scenes.objectiveen: Local inclination changes of the selected billboard support column.
scenes.pointen: An approved rigid position on the support column, outside electrical parts, lifting areas and sign-maintenance access.
scenes.briefen: Sign and support IDs, mounting arrangement, site access, number of monitored supports and the inspection-relevant angle change.
scenes.alten: Single-column roadside billboard with its full support pole, blank sign panel, base area and surrounding road visible.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.

title: Industrial & logistics supports
introen: Fixed conveyor columns, production-line frames and pump skids, identified point by point for routine maintenance review.

scenes.title: Fixed conveyor supports
scenes.en: Cover selected fixed conveyor columns with basic inclination points along a factory or distribution line. Associate each point with a line section and support ID, then compare it with the commissioned posture. This gives maintenance teams a consistent way to review a changed support after layout work, handling contact or servicing, while extending economical point coverage across a long installation.
scenes.measureen: Inclination changes at selected fixed conveyor-support columns.
scenes.objectiveen: Inclination changes at selected fixed conveyor-support columns.
scenes.pointen: A rigid fixed support member, outside belts, rollers, moving loads and maintenance access clearances.
scenes.briefen: Conveyor layout, support IDs, fixed reference positions, handling exposure and the number of points needed along the line.
scenes.alten: Long fixed conveyor installation inside a factory, with its inclined conveyor section and multiple supporting steel columns visible.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.

scenes.title: Production-line support frames
scenes.en: Add basic tilt observations to selected fixed frames along a production line where broad asset coverage matters more than fine alignment measurement. Use a line, station and frame ID for each point, with a repeatable installation reference. Maintenance teams can compare persistent posture changes after a station is moved, a support is adjusted or the line layout is altered.
scenes.measureen: Local inclination of selected fixed production-line frame members against their installation reference.
scenes.objectiveen: Local inclination of selected fixed production-line frame members against their installation reference.
scenes.pointen: An approved rigid frame member, clear of machine travel, process connections, service panels and routine operator access.
scenes.briefen: Line and station layout, selected frame IDs, relocation history, point count and the angle changes meaningful to the maintenance team.
scenes.alten: Wide factory production line with repeated fixed machine frames, workstations, overhead services and a clear aisle.
scenes.source: V4 user-confirmed positioning: economical fixed-asset inclination monitoring, with an asset-specific installation baseline; representative application illustration.

scenes.title: Pump-skid frames
scenes.en: Keep an inclination reference for pump-skid frames distributed across a facility. Tie each point to the pump set and skid ID so maintenance teams can review a changed base posture after servicing, relocation or work on the supporting foundation. A modest set of points across several skids supports an organised equipment record, using comparisons under similar stationary conditions.
scenes.measureen: Stationary inclination changes of the pump set’s rigid skid frame.
scenes.objectiveen: Stationary inclination changes of the pump set’s rigid skid frame.
scenes.pointen: A rigid member of the skid base, away from rotating parts, hot surfaces, pipe connections and service access.
scenes.briefen: Pump and skid IDs, base arrangement, comparable measurement conditions, servicing history and the points planned across the facility.
scenes.alten: Industrial pump and motor mounted on a steel skid above a concrete base, with surrounding pipework and factory space visible.

title: Campus & utility facilities

Give each cabinet and sensing point a location ID, then compare later readings with the installed reference. scenes.objectiveen: Inclination changes of the fixed cabinet body or its supporting base frame.
scenes.pointen: A rigid non-opening part of the cabinet body or base, preserving seals and clear of doors, locks and cable entries.
scenes.briefen: Cabinet inventory, base details, locations, maintenance access and the point coverage needed across the outdoor site.
scenes.alten: Freestanding outdoor utility cabinets on fixed bases in a landscaped equipment compound, with full enclosures and their surroundings visible.
